subject: Pilot: OrbitWorks SDK -> Redwood lightweight proxy for telemetry
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@orbitworks.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 3 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot request — OrbitWorks SDK lightweight proxy for Redwood telemetry

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the intro call last week. OrbitWorks builds a client SDK that many SaaS partners embed to run vector searches and prompt orchestration. Several of our joint prospects have asked for a lightweight way to forward SDK-level traces and prompt metadata into Redwood so they can view end-to-end latency and token attribution in the same console.

We think a small proxy component that ships with the SDK would be the lowest-friction path: the SDK POSTs batched telemetry to the proxy, the proxy forwards an authenticated envelope to Redwood’s telemetry ingest endpoint. Key asks from OrbitWorks:
- Minimal token/profile surface in the SDK (we prefer not to store long-lived customer keys).
- Ability to opt in per-customer and to redact prompt text where required.
- A sandbox flow so our engineers can validate delivery and sampling rates.

Attached is a short primer describing our SDK shapes and suggested sample payloads (orbit_sdk_integration_primer.pdf). Could Redwood share a checklist for required fields and a short sandbox URL we can hit? We’d love to run a 4–6 week pilot with a single joint customer and then expand.

Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Partnerships, OrbitWorks
samira@orbitworks.ai

Subject: Re: Pilot request — OrbitWorks SDK lightweight proxy for Redwood telemetry

Hi Samira — thanks, this is a great starter. Happy to run the pilot. High-level proposal from our side:

Phase 0 — Spec alignment (1 week)
- Redwood provides a minimal "telemetry envelope" spec (required fields, sampling hint, redaction flags) and a sandbox endpoint with a short-lived ingest key.
- OrbitWorks shares example SDK payloads and where redaction hooks live.

Phase 1 — Sandbox POC (2 weeks)
- OrbitWorks runs SDK + proxy against Redwood sandbox. We validate delivery, event shapes, sampling, and basic QA.
- Redwood provides an acceptance test harness (small script) to verify events landed and token attribution matches.

Phase 2 — Joint-customer pilot (4 weeks)
- One joint customer, controlled rollout, metrics collection. We monitor latency impact, token accounting, and SLOs.

Phase 3 — Production ramp + docs
- Expand to more customers, publish integration guide, and add a config knob in the Redwood Console for partner proxies.

Open questions from our side:
1) Do you want the proxy to perform any on-the-fly tokenization / deduping, or just forward batched events?
2) For customers who request redaction, do you prefer client-side redaction (SDK) or proxy-side?
3) Any legal/procurement constraints we should flag up front?

I attached a checklist we typically send partners (redwood_instrumentation-checklist.xlsx) — contains required event fields, schema examples, and our sandbox URL + short-lived key instructions. Proposed timeline: spec alignment this week, sandbox by Aug 17, pilot kickoff Aug 24. Does that work for you and your engineering lead?

If it helps I can block a 30-min joint sync later this week — Vanessa, Marissa, Karthik, any availability for Thursday morning PT?

Best,
Olga
Senior Partner Engineer
Redwood Inference

- We should confirm the commercial guardrail: pilot is free but any extended usage > 90 days or > 10M tokens should move to a short-term consumption agreement. I can handle contracting but need a scoping doc.
